title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a title or heading sheet for the folder. It has no proofs or computations. It names two topics.

(i) Duality of Dieudonné modules for Barsotti–Tate groups that are dual to each other. Take a p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) group G over a field k of characteristic p > 0, its Cartier/Serre dual G^*, and their contravariant Dieudonné modules M(G) and M(G^*) over the Witt vectors W(k). Then there is a canonical perfect pairing M(G) × M(G^*) → W(k), up to a Frobenius twist depending on conventions. Under this pairing F on one side is adjoint to V on the other, so M(G^*) ≅ M(G)^∨ with F and V interchanged.

(ii) The 'reduced Dieudonné module' M ⊗_W k = M/pM. This is the Dieudonné module of the truncated group G[p], with the induced F_0 and V_0. The next page identifies it intrinsically with H(G) = Lie(\tilde G^*), the Lie algebra of the universal vector extension of the dual. That is the first de Rham / crystalline cohomology of G. It comes with its Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → H(G) → t_{G^*} → 0, where ω_G = Ker F_0 = Im V_0.

The programme announced here is carried out on the following pages. Those pages show that the extensions for t_{\tilde G} and t_{\tilde G^*} are canonically transposed, with F_0 and V_0 exchanged. They then characterise infinitesimal G (resp. G^*) by nilpotence of F_0 (resp. V_0).

This serves Grothendieck's 1969–70 programme of an intrinsic, crystalline Dieudonné theory over arbitrary bases. In that programme the Dieudonné crystal is built from the Lie algebra of the universal extension.

ideas.what: Duality between the Dieudonné modules of a BT group and of its Cartier dual (F and V interchanged under a canonical pairing)
ideas.modern_name: Duality theorem for (crystalline) Dieudonné modules: D(G^*) ≅ D(G)^∨
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical over perfect fields (Dieudonné, Manin, Oda); over general bases Berthelot–Breen–Messing (Théorie de Dieudonné cristalline II, 1982)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, ICM Nice 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'; Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974) — stated there as part of the programme

ideas.what: Reduced Dieudonné module M⊗_W k, identified (next page) with the Lie algebra of the universal extension of G^*, carrying a Hodge filtration
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné module of G[p] / first de Rham cohomology of a BT group; Hodge filtration ω_G ⊂ D(G)_k

deep.surprise_reason: This is a near-blank cover page with only a two-line statement of topics. Both topics are standard and well documented, partly in Grothendieck's own 1970 announcements.
transcription_corrections: The first word 'Dualité' appears overwritten or corrected in the image (the 'D' was retraced); the reading is otherwise correct.
'Le' at the start of the fourth line is written in heavier ink, apparently added or retraced. The text is 'Le module de Dieudonné réduit M⊗_W k' — the transcription is accurate.
